title: Deep learning enhances the prediction of HLA class I-presented CD8+ T cell epitopes in foreign pathogens
one_line: Introduces MUNIS, a bimodal deep learning model trained on over 650,000 HLA class I ligands that predicts peptide-HLAI binding and antigen processing to nominate CD8+ T cell epitopes, validated experimentally on Epstein-Barr virus.
key_claims: MUNIS uses a two-part architecture, one component predicting peptide binding to HLAI molecules and one modelling antigen processing, trained on more than 650,000 HLAI ligands.
MUNIS outperforms existing epitope prediction tools in cross-validation benchmarks.
Applied to Epstein-Barr virus, MUNIS recovered known epitopes and identified novel ones confirmed in laboratory experiments.
MUNIS-predicted EBV epitopes elicited both effector and memory CD8+ T cell responses.
MUNIS predictions performed comparably to experimental peptide-HLA stability assays.
limitations: Prediction of immunogenicity, as distinct from presentation, remains imperfect.
Coverage is restricted to a subset of HLA variants, limiting applicability across diverse populations.
The model lacks sufficient T cell receptor data to fully connect presentation to T cell recognition.
Experimental validation was demonstrated in a single pathogen context (EBV) rather than across many pathogens.
open_questions: Does adding paired TCR repertoire data to MUNIS convert presentation prediction into reliable immunogenicity prediction?
Can performance be sustained on HLA alleles under-represented in the 650,000-ligand training set?
Would prospective testing against an emerging pathogen confirm the claimed pandemic-preparedness utility?
